## 🤖 AI review — `ai-review:changes`

### Reviewer
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: pass
blocking: 0
summary: Spec-only change (SPEC-060 PROPOSED Amendment A + new specifying-status SPEC-135); internally consistent, code citations verified accurate, no duplicate id, no stubs/secrets, invariants addressed at spec level.
findings:
- info specs/minspec/SPEC-135-self-installing-build/requirements.md INV-3 — INV-3 (blast radius) rests on an interpretive judgment — treating the founder's one-time host setup act as a machine's opt-in marker in place of a repo-root .minspec/. The spec correctly surfaces this for founder ratification via approval rather than deciding it silently, so it is not a defect, but it is the one genuinely load-bearing assumption the approver must consciously accept before any host-service code is built.
- info specs/minspec/SPEC-060-build-provenance-stamp/requirements.md Amendment A — Merging the amendment changes SPEC-060's file bytes, staling its approval and (per the spec's own 'What it costs' and spec-gate behaviour) denying agent edits to the six files SPEC-060 declares under implements:/affects: until the founder re-approves. This is acknowledged and intended, but reviewers/the funnel should expect those files to be frozen for agents in the interim (tracked: #1079).
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

### Architect (design / scope)
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: changes
blocking: 1
summary: Thorough, well-recorded spec pair, but SPEC-135 reinterprets constitution invariant 3 / DR-074 (machine-wide write) by spec approval alone with "No new record", asymmetric with its own DR-065 amendment track.
findings:
- blocking specs/minspec/SPEC-135-self-installing-build/requirements.md (INV-3 and "Decision records") — SPEC-135 registers a per-user background service — a write to a machine-wide surface (`~/.config/systemd/user/`, crontab, or launchd) that DR-074 decision 3 names as out of bounds ("MinSpec does not write them"). INV-3 concedes DR-074 "states that bound with no exception for an owner's own act" and asks that "Approving this spec accepts that reading," while the Decision records section records "No new record for the rest." This reinterprets a never-violate constitution invariant and an in-force…
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

### Skeptic (evidence discipline)
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: pass
blocking: 0
summary: Both files are honest Specify-phase proposals (SPEC-135 status: specifying, Amendment A labelled PROPOSED-not-accepted); every file:line citation I spot-checked is accurate and no feature is falsely claimed built.
findings:
- low specs/minspec/SPEC-060-build-provenance-stamp/requirements.md (Amendment A, "What it costs") and SPEC-135 ("Context", host-facts tables) — Several "Measured 2026-10-09" claims — the spec-gate allow/deny-for-all-six matrix, the git 2.43.0 fast-forward table, and the 19-vs-9 commit recount — are environment measurements not reproducible from the diff itself; they rest on the author's say-so. Non-blocking: each is honestly dated and framed as a measurement, and every adjacent claim carrying a file:line anchor (build-provenance.ts:141, extension.ts:756-791, build-extension.sh:29-31, build-provenance.test.ts:33-54, SPEC-060 status: pla…
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

_Independent fresh-context reviewers (`scripts/review-branch.sh`, no-tools agents reading the diff as untrusted data); each label decided by the deterministic fail-closed gate (`scripts/review-decide.sh`). Posted by `minspec-sdd[bot]` from CI — provenance is the App identity, verified here, not the label alone (#428, #342). Coverage `panel` — voters that ran: **reviewer + architect + skeptic**. Did NOT run: **security** — docs-only change: every changed file is Markdown, so there is no code surface to review. The combined verdict fails toward `changes` if ANY voter requests changes._

Documented intentional cost and matches the SPEC-044 Amendment A precedent, so non-blocking — flagged for awareness of the cross-work side effect (#1079).

Correctly held behind #2632 before part C is built, so architecturally sound at Specify phase — noted so reviewers of the eventual DR-074 amendment treat it as the real gate for the host service.

commits.messageBody:
…follows it

Specify-phase requirements only: one new file, no design.md, no tasks.md, no
code. It carries the founder's decision of 2026-10-09 on #2203 (no host-side
check for installed extension staleness): "auto", then "another part of auto
that i'd like to see is watching for new git changes and pulling them
automatically."

Root cause, from the diagnosis on #2203: every actor that fast-forwards the
dogfood checkout moves it past the installed build without building or
installing anything, and the only gate on the skew is a toast inside the
editor, because the extension records its running build nowhere outside its
own process.

Five parts, as decided:
1. The extension writes which build each window runs into the ignored
   directory its heartbeat already uses, so agents can read it.
2. The drain builds when a packed path changes on main, from a clean checkout
   of that commit, and not behind the quota gate.
3. One setup act on the host registers a per-user service. After it, each
   published build installs with no prompt.
4. SPEC-060 (build provenance stamp) Amendment A, in the next commit, stops
   docs-only commits warning (#2616).
5. The same service fetches and fast-forwards the checkout, no further than
   the installed build covers. No stash, autostash, reset or rebase: a pull
   that would change an uncommitted file does not move at all.

Measured while writing, on throwaway repositories with git 2.43.0: a plain
merge --ff-only leaves unrelated dirty and untracked files byte-identical;
refuses whole when an incoming commit changes a dirty path, even with
identical bytes; and passes identical copies once those paths are staged,
without rewriting them (same inode and mtime).

Relation to DR-065 (presence-gated fast-forward): extend. The record needs an
amendment before the pull is built, filed as #2628.

Three choices are recorded with a recommendation and its cost, for approval
to ratify: when a new build starts running, whether an identical uncommitted
approval holds the pull, and which process pulls.

Id: 135 is the highest claimed plus one across origin/main at 1bc9e484, the
32 open pull requests, all 257 remote-tracking branches and every local ref.

Refs #2203, #2616. Filed from this work: #2628, #2629, #2626.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.messageBody:
… path make a build stale

Proposes an amendment to SPEC-060 (build provenance stamp), in the form
SPEC-044 Amendment A used: one appended section before Traceability, the
label in the heading and no body status line, so the status-parity gate
still reads one status for the file. Nothing else in the file is touched.

What it changes: FR-3's trigger and AC-4's fixture are narrowed from "HEAD is
ahead of the running build" to "a commit after the stamp changes a packed
path", and the warning counts only those. Recounted on 2026-10-09: of the 19
commits behind in the warning the founder saw, 9 change a packed path, and
the last move of his checkout before it carried none. Three criteria are
added: the silent case, the fall-back when the filtered count cannot be
trusted, and a test tying the packed-path list to the build's own inputs.

This voids the current approval by design, and that has a cost that is
larger than #2616 measured. Running scripts/hooks/spec-gate.py against the
file before and after: allow for all six declared files before, deny for all
six after (an undeclared file is allow both times). The six are the three
under implements: and the three under affects:, which are spec.ts,
lifecycle.ts and scripts/dispatch-issue.sh. So from the moment this reaches
main until the founder re-approves SPEC-060, agent edits to those files are
denied. The hash moves from c01e2a84... to 2395da3e..., and the spec derives
specifying while its status line still reads planning.

The amendment says how it becomes accepted (a current approval of this file,
not an edit to its heading), which is the gap #2613 records for the four
existing blocks of this kind.

Written with SPEC-135 (self-installing build), which builds, installs and
pulls on the same question.

Refs #2616, #2203.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.messageBody:
…the record must say it

Review finding on pull request 2631 (architect, blocking): the first draft
had INV-3 concede that DR-074 (blast radius is the project) puts machine-wide
surfaces out of bounds with no exception for an owner's own act, and then
asked that approving the spec accept a reading under which the one-time host
setup act is the machine's opt-in, while the Decision records section said
no new record was needed. That reinterprets a constitution invariant and an
in-force record by spec approval alone, and it was asymmetric with the same
spec's treatment of DR-065, which it sends to an amendment.

Fixed by putting both on the same track:

- INV-3 no longer asks approval to accept a reading. It says the question is
  the record's, that the registration is not built until DR-074 answers it,
  and what moves if the answer is no (the act prints the registration and the
  founder installs it himself; one clause of FR-10).
- Decision records now names two amendments, each its own act and each due
  before the part that leans on it is built: DR-065 before the pull, DR-074
  before the registration. The DR-074 one is filed as #2632, with the
  recommended answer and that answer's cost.
- The DR-065 section says the same in the same words: approving the spec
  does not amend the record.
- The cost section says what was implicit: the installed build serves every
  project opened in that editor, and they now get each merged build without
  a chosen moment.

Refs #2203, #2632, #2628.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
